Postgraduate MSc Professional Experience option available Accounting and Finance Take your career to the next level. Develop your financial skills and know-how with our comprehensive Masters in Accounting and Finance. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event MSc Professional Experience MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location Chelmsford Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time Course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), or 15 months (January and May starts). The Professional Experience option takes 24 months (September starts), or 27 months (January starts). Professional Experience Start date September 2027 January 2027 Location Chelmsford Award MSc Duration 2 years with professional experience Course durations vary slightly: 12 months (September starts), or 15 months (January and May starts). The Professional Experience option takes 24 months (September starts), or 27 months (January starts). 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 If you’re driven to succeed in the ever-changing, innovative world of accounting and finance, this is the course for you. At ARU in Chelmsford, you’ll gain an understanding of global financial markets and the complexity of the industry. You’ll learn the most up-to-date practices alongside classmates from around the world in dynamic seminars and our Bloomberg Financial Market Lab, where you can learn the trade in a safe, supportive space. Accredited by ACCA Our Accounting and Finance degree is accredited by ACCA, which means you’ll be exempted from the five Applied Knowledge and Skills papers of the ACCA qualification. Why ARU? Gain a thorough understanding of global financial markets Collaborate with classmates from around the world Develop your analytical and trading skills in our Bloomberg Financial Market Lab Build your network with our industry contacts and guest speakers Enhance your employability with our optional Professional Experience year Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers A Master’s in Accounting and Finance opens a wealth of doors, in the UK and internationally. Working on the more analytical side of finance, or in forensic accounting, are just a couple of paths you might consider. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a research programme at ARU, such as our Business PhD - School of Economics, Finance and Law . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Studying accounting and finance is about understanding the language of business. It equips you with the analytical skills to make sound financial decisions. Laura Muncey, Deputy Head of School Gain a thorough understanding of international accounting and markets. You’ll explore international accounting and international financial markets, focussing on investment analysis and portfolio management. You’ll also look at corporate finance and financial strategies of organisations in the capital, financial and operational markets. In addition, you’ll study tax in theory and practice, learning how to provide tax advice, solve issues, and conduct audits professionally. You’ll top off your Master’s with your Postgraduate Major Project. Supervised by one of our expert academics, you’ll use suitable research methods to propose solutions to one or more problems in a relevant area of your choice. What will I study? MSc Professional Experience MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 International Financial Markets and Investment International Accounting Applied Corporate Finance and Financial Strategy UK Taxation and Auditing Postgraduate Major Project Module details Professional Experience You can choose to study with us over two years (full-time), and take Professional Experience modules in Year 2, with a Preparation for Professional Experience module in Year 1. Professional experience modules Professional Project * Professional Project 2 * Professional Work Placement * Professional Work Experience * Module details What are Professional Experience modules? Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Accounting and Finance assessed? We’ll assess your progress in a number of ways, mainly through informal question and answer sessions. You can also expect individual and group presentations, management reports, exams, presentation or written analysis of case studies, and assignments. Our assessment strategy is linked closely to your employability. You'll develop skills that can be transferred to the professional environment such as teamwork, communication and presentation skills, and the ability to work under pressure. Who teaches Accounting and Finance at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Dr Lenka Krupová Senior Lecturer Dr Wei Kang Senior Lecturer in Accounting and Finance Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . You can also access support, should you need it, with study skills, health and wellbeing, and more. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Postgraduate MSc Accounting and Financial Management Gain comprehensive understanding of the theoretical and practical aspects of accounting and finance at ARU London. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now MSc 2 years part-time MSc Start date September 2027 January 2027 May 2027 Location ARU London Award MSc Duration 1 year full-time 2 years part-time It's possible for UK students to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. Develop the skills, knowledge and competencies necessary to evaluate financial information, analyse financial statements, value companies and make informed decisions. You'll gain an understanding of the regulatory framework that governs accounting and finance practices and comply with relevant laws and regulations, and build your analytical, critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making skills through real-world accounting and finance applications. You'll also learn how to think and act as a global citizen by taking ethical, social and environmental considerations into account. Careers Prepare for a range of careers in the accounting and finance industry. You'll graduate with the in-demand skills and knowledge required to make informed financial decisions in today's rapidly changing and complex business environment. Whether you decide to go into investment banking, risk management, financial analysis, or consultancy, you'll be able to apply key transferable skills such as critical thinking, problem-solving, communication, teamwork and leadership. Teaching and modules At ARU London, we understand that the financial function of an organisation is the foundation of a dynamic and resilient business model. Through practical projects, case studies, simulations and experiential learning activities, you'll gain hands-on experience across the accounting and finance spectrum. Our inclusive curriculum also offers you opportunities to develop your critical thinking, problem-solving, communication, teamwork and leadership skills, preparing you to meet challenges and contribute to organisational growth and success. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Postgraduate Major Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic that interests you. What will I study? MSc 2 years part-time MSc Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Postgraduate Study Skills, Research Methods, and Ethics Corporate Reporting, Budgeting and Control Corporate Finance and Valuations Taxation, Audit and Assurance Investment and Risk Management Postgraduate Major Project (Accounting and Finance) Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. How is Accounting and Financial Management assessed? We'll assess you through assignments, presentations, and examinations, as well as your Major Project, which involves detailed research, analysis and reporting of a finance related issue. Facilities As a student at ARU London you'll have access to: over 30 lecture theatres ranging in size from those that can accommodate up to 200 students in a theatre-style seating arrangement, to others that are perfect for highly interactive seminars two interconnected buildings with libraries containing core texts, wider reading materials, printers, and computer labs. There are also multiple study pods and booths for group work or personal study. You’ll be supported by: our Employability Service, helping you develop skills, knowledge, and experience through a range of extra-curricular sessions and career-focused support experienced wellbeing advisors and counsellors, offering assistance with mental, physical, medical, and/or learning conditions a mobile app giving you 24/7 access to learning resources, the e-library, and your timetable. Throughout this course you’ll conduct research in our Science Centre labs and develop the skills to design, execute, and critically analyse scientific projects independently and collaboratively. You’ll benefit from strong industry links within the Cambridge life sciences network and graduate ready to contribute confidently to modern biomedical research and healthcare diagnostics. Course Director Dr Grisha Pirianov introduces our Master's courses in Advanced Biomedical Science, Applied Bioscience, Biotechnology, and Molecular Microbiology. Close full-screen gallery. Course Director Dr Grisha Pirianov introduces our Master's courses in Advanced Biomedical Science, Applied Bioscience, Biotechnology, and Molecular Microbiology. Why ARU? Gain hands-on experience in advanced molecular and tissue culture labs mirroring real healthcare environments Learn directly from internationally renowned biomedical scientists Study in Cambridge, a global hub for life sciences research and biotechnology Design, execute and analyse complex biomedical research projects using advanced scientific methods Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Graduate well-prepared for careers in biomedical research, diagnostics, healthcare science and the pharmaceutical sector. You’ll also build key transferable skills like critical thinking, scientific writing, teamwork, and presenting that will boost your employability across science, product development, marketing and more. You’ll benefit from guest speakers from public and private bioscience sectors' real-world career insights, helping you explore diverse opportunities in the field. What can you do with an Advanced Biomedical Science degree? You’ll be well-prepared for a range of specialist and multidisciplinary careers across healthcare, research and industry. You could progress into roles such as biomedical scientist, research associate, clinical trials specialist or a laboratory manager, applying your advanced knowledge of human disease, molecular mechanisms and diagnostic technologies to improve healthcare outcomes. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a PhD programme at ARU, such as our MPhil/PhD Biomedical Science . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our course will enhance your knowledge, strengthen your practical and employability skills, and equip you for a successful professional career in the Cambridge industrial cluster. Dr Grisha Pirianov, Course Director You’ll explore contemporary medical diagnostics, including antimicrobial developments and translational medicine. You'll learn practical pathology techniques used in real NHS labs while developing professional skills in ethics, communication, and teamwork, alongside bioinformatics and molecular biology techniques. Finally, you’ll prepare and carry out a substantial research project, gaining experience in experimental design, data collection and analysis, and scientific communication, all vital for a successful career in biomedical science. Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Advanced Biomedical Science assessed? Assessment will be based upon a varied and integrated assessment strategy which will include portfolio, presentations, poster preparation, case studies and problem-solving exercises. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 As climate change, resource scarcity and global food insecurity challenge traditional systems, they also unlock vast opportunities for innovation, impact and growth. On this MBA, you’ll develop the systems-based approach, sustainability insight, and digital fluency to meet these challenges. At the same time, you’ll develop your management skills, with a focus on strategy, decision-making, and leading people through times of change that require them to reskill, upskill, and adapt. Why ARU? Learn how to build more resilient and sustainable food systems Explore regenerative business models and circular economy thinking Gain digital and leadership skills, and the know-how to drive change Apply your knowledge to real-world challenges through live projects and industry collaboration Study on a campus with a history of agricultural excellence Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Prepare to take on leadership roles in a rapidly changing industry. You’ll graduate with critical skills in sustainability, circular economics and strategic management, opening doors to careers in agribusiness, food supply chains, policy and sustainability consulting. Through hands-on projects and guidance from industry experts, you’ll gain the confidence to drive innovation, improve productivity and support sustainable growth in food systems worldwide. What can you do with an Agribusiness degree? You'll be equipped for senior management, consultancy or policy-making roles within multinational food brands, agritech firms and environmental agencies. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. Where have previous Agribusiness graduates worked? Our graduates have gone on to strategic corporate roles within international commodity trading companies, agricultural infrastructure firms, supply chain logistics specialists and sustainable food consultancy practices. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Teaching and modules This MBA equips future agricultural leaders with the economic insight and agri-tech innovation skills to drive sustainable food systems. Dr Rob Gowers, Course Director Learn and apply professional skills as you explore sustainable food systems. You’ll focus on the efficient use of resources, postharvest practices and supply chain management to reduce waste and environmental impact. You’ll analyse food security challenges, global sustainability goals, and innovative strategies such as Controlled Environment Agriculture. You’ll also evaluate current food systems and propose resilient, context-specific solutions for the future of agri-food production and global food security. You’ll complete your MBA with your dissertation – a substantial research project on a relevant topic of your choice. What will I study? Year 1 Sustainable Global Business Management and Circular Economics (15 credits) Postharvest Systems Management (15 credits) Food Marketing and Value Chain Management (15 credits) Applied Research (Methods) for Managers (15 credits) Food Security and Sustainable Farm Management (15 credits) Strategic Management (15 credits) Controlled Environment Agriculture (15 credits) Leading Sustainable Change Strategies and Innovation in Food Systems (15 credits) Postgraduate Major Project (60 credits) Into ARU Module details 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. Currently, this course is taught in intensive, structured blocks on Tuesdays and Thursdays. How is Agribusiness assessed? You'll be assessed through a variety of methods, reflecting our focus on case studies, data and research. These include written research-style papers and reports for commercial enterprises, debates, discussions, presentations, time constrained exercises and group work. Who teaches Agribusiness at ARU? Postgraduate Biology MPhil, PhD Research ( full-time, part-time) Cambridge January 2027, April, September 2027 Apply online For application deadlines visit our how to apply page . Overview As a postgraduate researcher you will join an interdisciplinary group, within the School of Life Sciences, which is well-connected with industry and fellow research institutions worldwide. PhD candidates are encouraged to take an active role in the School's research community in areas currently spanning global change ecology, conservation and animal behaviour and welfare. Full description We have a large multidisciplinary academic team ready to support you in your studies working across our two groups, Applied Ecology Research Group (AERG) and Behavioural Ecology Research Group . By combining this expertise with wider specialisms we’ve been able to create exciting projects addressing today’s key issues. As a result our research has had real impact on the human-dominated and ‘natural’ landscapes, from furthering scientific understanding to shaping environmental policy and practice. In the Applied Ecology Research Group our primary focus is to assess, understand and mitigate anthropogenic impacts such as plastic pollution, climate change, invasive species, agriculture and urbanisation, on biodiversity and ecosystem services in terrestrial, freshwater and marine ecosystems. We use a range of modern tools, including ecological network analysis, ecosystem modelling, satellite tracking and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) along with interdisciplinary techniques, such as combining the disciplines of biology and ecology with molecular biology, biogeochemistry and microbiology. The Behavioural Ecology Research Group are an active community with core areas of interest currently including animal communication, cognition, social behaviour, and animal welfare. We cover a wide range of study organisms, including mammals, birds, insects, crustaceans, fish and cephalopods. Our research involves fieldwork in many countries and we also carry out work in museums, zoos, and laboratories. With our wide-ranging expertise we're well-placed to provide the specialist supervision you need for your project, within an inspiring research community that values and involves its postgraduates. As part of your programme you’ll enjoy formal research training and opportunities to gain experience working with conservation NGOs and others based in Cambridge. There will be opportunities to present your work and represent us at internal, national and international scientific conferences, and you'll be fully immersed in the groups research activities. We also encourage cross-discipline interaction with other research groups in our University. In addition to our Biology PhD, we've also identified a range of innovative research project opportunities for you as a postgraduate researcher. Completion dates MPhil: full-time 1-3 years, part-time 2-4 years. PhD via progression from MPhil, including that period: full-time 2.5-5 years, part-time 3.5-6 years. PhD: full-time 2-4 years, part-time 3-6 years. For further guidance on the duration of research degrees please refer to the Research Degrees Regulations . Biology PhD project opportunities Reducing the impact of single-use plastics Sustainable Futures Research theme Supervision and support We’ll provide high-quality supervision formally and informally, so you can get the most from your programme – and we’ll fully involve you in our calendar of research meetings, seminars and workshops. Our supervisory staff are recognised experts in their field. Their research expertise includes: Dr Alvin Helden – Alvin is interested in the biodiversity of habitats in urban and agricultural areas and in restored ecosystems. He specialises in insects, particularly leafhoppers and other true bugs (Hemiptera). Dr Andrew Smith – Andrew’s main areas of expertise are behavioural ecology and primate colour vision. His work looks at how animals, from aardvarks to goldfish, interact with each other and their environment. Dr Çağlar Akçay – Çağlar is interested in the role communication plays in animal social behaviour, with a focus on the interaction of evolution and development of communication systems. His research is mostly focused on songbirds. Dr Claudia Wascher – Claudia is experienced in social cognition and physiology, interested in the evolution of cooperation as well as costs and benefits of social behaviour. Dr Dannielle Green – Dannielle is an ecologist interested in all aspects of ecology but her main research focus has been on examining how human activities affect the health of individual organisms and the biodiversity and functioning of marine habitats. Dr Dawn Hawkins – Dawn has over 20 years’ experience in curriculum development and teaching whole organism biology and statistics in higher education. Dr Hannah White – Hannah is macroecologist interested in how biodiversity is distributed in space and time. Her research often focuses on species traits and how these vary between ecological communities. Dr Helen Wheeler – Helen is a wildlife ecologist, focused on vertebrate systems in northern, alpine and Arctic environments. Her research is interdisciplinary, exploring both ecological and social aspects of wildlife change. Dr Jacob Dunn – Jacob is a behavioural ecologist, broadly interested in the biology and evolution of communication systems in humans and other animals (mostly primates). Dr Jim Littlemore – Jim is an experienced Chartered ecologist with broad research interests in sustainable land management, recreation ecology, habitat restoration and novel ecological surveying methods for British fauna. Dr Joseph Bailey – Joseph’s work explores the relationship between biodiversity and geodiversity (surface and subsurface materials, landforms, and processes) to advance ecological theory, biodiversity modelling, and practical conservation. Dr Krishna Balasubramaniam – Krishna is a behavioural and infectious disease ecologist. He is interested in the ecology and evolution of animal social behaviour, human-wildlife interactions, and their effects on zoonotic microbes. Dr Marian Bond – Marian has over 30 years' experience of working and teaching in animal behaviour and physiotherapy. She’s a fellow of the Society of Biology, a professional dog trainer and a PADI-certified Master Diver. Dr Paty Celis – Paty’s research expertise is in evolutionary biology with a particular focus on behavioural and molecular ecology. Dr Peter Brown – Peter’s key area of research is ladybird ecology. He’s joint scheme organiser of the UK Ladybird Survey and co-author of two recent books on ladybirds. Dr Philip Pugh – Philip teaches on our BSc (Hons) Marine Biology with Biodiversity and Conservation course. His recent research has centred on Antarctic biogeography, cladistics and multivariate analysis. Dr Rachael Miller (Harrison) – Rachael is a comparative psychologist, broadly interested in the evolution of cognition and behaviour in humans and other animals (mostly birds), as well as applications of this research for animal conservation and welfare. Dr Sarah J Hart – Sarah’s main areas of expertise are in forest entomology & mycology, chemical ecology and animal physiology & behaviour. Dr Thomas Ings – Thomas is an ecologist whose research interests include pollinator behaviour, invertebrate community ecology and conservation. His key aim is to develop an understanding of how community structure is influenced by individual traits, including behaviour. Where you'll research Your faculty The Faculty of Science & Engineering is one of the largest of the four faculties at ARU. Whether you choose to study with us full-time or part-time, on campus or at a distance, there’s an option whatever your level – from a foundation degree, BSc, MSc, PhD or professional doctorate. Whichever course you pick, you’ll gain the theory and practical skills needed to progress with confidence. Join us and you could find yourself learning in the very latest laboratories or on field trips or work placements with well-known and respected companies. You may even have the opportunity to study abroad. Everything we do in the faculty has a singular purpose: to provide a world-class environment to create, share and advance knowledge in science, technology and engineering fields. This is key to all of our futures. Visit your faculty Where can I study? Cambridge Our campus is close to the centre of Cambridge, often described as the perfect student city. Explore our Cambridge campus Fees & funding Course fees UK students, 2026/27 (per year) £5,238 UK students, 2026/27 (part-time, per year) £2,619 International students, 2026/27 (per year) £17,500 International students, 2026/27 (part-time, per year) £8,750 Bench fees In some cases extra costs known as bench fees will be charged for a postgraduate research degree. These are to cover additional/exceptional costs directly related to a specific research project. Some examples of these costs are (the list is not exhaustive): equipment hire, access costs to specialist equipment/workshops, volunteer expenses, specialist tissue/cell culture, specialist reagents or materials, specialist software, access to specialist databases, data collection costs, specialist media, recording or digital storage needs. We charge bench fees in bands. They may apply for every year of your course. These bands are the same for full- and part-time students. If you have to pay bench fees this will be made clear at your interview, and stated in your offer letter. For 2026/27 the bench fee bands are: £500 £1,400 £2,400 £4,900 £9,800 PhD by Published Work Initial registration: £1,700 Full registration: £4,900 Writing up fees 2026/27 £1,400 How do I pay my fees? You can pay your fees upfront, in full or in instalments – though you won't need to pay until you've accepted an offer to study with us. Find out more about paying your fees . Funding For advice on the Doctoral Loan and other sources of funding, including ARU scholarships, visit our finance guide for postgraduate researchers . You might also find The Alternative Guide to Postgraduate Funding helpful. ARU research ARU's academic excellence was recognised in 2021, as part of the Research Excellence Framework (REF), an exercise which assesses the quality of academic research. Sixteen areas of our work were classed as generating world-leading research . The results showed that we're making a significant impact on the societies we live in. Careers There are opportunities in our field for you to combine studying with working in an area relevant to your future career. This is especially so given that Cambridge is a major centre internationally for conservation non-government organisations and bodies such as The Cambridge Conservation Forum. You’ll also develop transferrable skills during your postgraduate research training, ranging from report-writing and presentation to statistical analysis and use of GIS packages. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Discover how an understanding of animal behaviour can help address global conservation challenges. By combining behavioural ecology, conservation biology and emerging technologies, this course equips you with practical research, data analysis and science communication skills. You'll gain hands-on experience applying animal behavioural science to real-world conservation issues alongside expert academics and environmental partners. Hear from our staff and students about studying Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation at ARU. Close full-screen gallery. Hear from our staff and students about studying Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation at ARU. Why ARU? Develop your expertise in animal behaviour through fieldwork, laboratory sessions and conservation projects Build career-defining research, technical and analytical skills in behavioural and conservation practice Work collaboratively with zoological collections and animal welfare organisations on real-world environmental projects and Live Briefs Conduct your major research project with supervision from leading academics from our Centre for Ecology, Evolution and Environment Enhance your field skills with an optional short course in France hosted by the Mediterranean Ecology Research Observatory for Practical Skills Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers This course expanded my technical knowledge for research and conservation and exposed me to several career paths I'd never considered. Noel Ellis, Graduate Ecologist, MKA Ecology Prepare to apply your understanding of animal behaviour to global conservation challenges. This course nurtures specialist scientific knowledge alongside practical research, analytical and communication skills valued across the animal and conservation sector. Through projects, fieldwork, lab sessions and professional networking opportunities, you'll graduate ready for a range of careers in conservation, research and animal science. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU, such as our PhD Biology . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with an Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation degree? Our Graduates pursue careers across wildlife conservation, environmental management, conservation biology, zoological collections, conservation charities and government agencies. Typical roles include: Conservation biologist Behavioural researcher Ecological consultant Conservation project officer Zoo conservation and education officer Environmental educator/community work Attending the 2025 Student Conference on Conservation Science Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation student Afrika shares her experiences of the 2025 Student Conference on Conservation Science (SCCS) in Cambridge. Where have previous Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation graduates worked? Recent graduates have built successful careers across the conservation sector, taking on roles such as: Marine Biologist, Benthic Solutions Aquarist, Sea Life Chalk Streams Project Officer, Cambridge City Council Data and Research Officer, Mammal Society Marine Biologist Expedition Guide, Hurtigruten Expeditions Teacher, Niagara University Fisheries Officer, Brown & May Marine Head of Conservation, Research & License, Woburn Safari Park Animal Technician, Agenda Life Sciences How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our PGT courses provide an opportunity to gain experience in real-world research environments. Prof Claudia Wascher, Professor or Behavioural Biology Explore how animal behaviour research informs modern conservation practice. You'll learn from internationally recognised experts in behavioural ecology, conservation genetics, animal welfare and global change ecology. Through lectures, workshops, laboratory classes, fieldwork and independent study, you'll develop skills in wildlife monitoring, GIS, genetics and quantitative analysis. You'll apply your learning to real-world conservation challenges, tailor your studies through specialist options and field courses, and complete an independent research project aligned with your interests and career goals. Understand the links between humans and nature conservation in the UK and abroad. Open a larger version of this image in full screen gallery. Learn how we can sustainably manage our land for wildlife. Open a larger version of this image in full screen gallery. Collect data on a range of species in the UK and abroad. Study at ARU in Writtle and drive positive change for the natural world. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 On this course, you’ll gain the scientific knowledge and hands-on experience you need to tackle current conservation challenges and shape the future of animal welfare and conservation. Taking an advanced, interdisciplinary approach to the biological, ethical and ecological factors that shape animal wellbeing, you’ll learn how ethical practice, human-animal relationships, and behaviour change can be leveraged to protect animals and the environments they depend on for generations to come. Why ARU? Focus on both animal welfare and conservation Learn from highly qualified staff involved in conservation and welfare projects Build your skills on a rural campus, with conservation areas and a working farm Work with livestock, exotic and companion animals Benefit from our relationships with Colchester Zoo, Essex Wildlife Trust and more Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers My time at ARU Writtle gave me the confidence and skills needed to further my career in animal welfare research. Alice King, MSc Animal Welfare and Conservation graduate Prepare for an impactful career promoting biodiversity and animal wellbeing. As well as vital scientific knowledge, research skills, and hands-on experience, you’ll graduate with an understanding of policy and legislation, and how behaviour change and community engagement can make a real difference in education, advocacy and conservation programmes. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with an Animal Welfare and Conservation degree? Graduates from this course are highly employable for management-level roles in welfare, conservation, and research across government, NGOs, zoos, rescue centres, and organisations like DEFRA, RSPCA, RSPB, Natural England, and NatureScot. Potential roles include: Senior government positions, e.g., DEFRA quarantine officers. Animal health inspector. Specialists in farm animal nutrition, pet food manufacturing, breeding, veterinary medicines and pharmaceuticals. Roles in animal welfare charities. Positions in zoos, safari parks, and animal rescue centres. Opportunities with independent wildlife and conservation agencies. Where have previous Animal Conservation and Welfare graduates worked? Graduates from this course have gone on to roles including: Ecologist at Cherryfield Ecology Ltd Animal Keeper at Longleat Production Manager at Dietex Sales Manager at Orffa Business Development Executive at Vet Vision AI Animal Welfare Officer at The Animal Rescue Charity (ARC) (Foxdells) How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Shape the future of animal welfare and conservation through scientific knowledge, practical experience, and real-world impact. Dr Sife Chinkunya, Course Director Dive into animal welfare, behaviour, nutrition, genetics and conservation. You’ll learn how diet impacts welfare in domestic, farm and zoo species, and develop skills in welfare inspection and nutritional assessment while getting hands-on with molecular techniques like PCR and electrophoresis. You’ll explore ethics, human-animal relationships and behavioural science for real-world welfare and conservation solutions. You’ll also gain practical experience in habitat management and biodiversity assessment. You’ll complete your Master’s with a Major Project – a substantial research project focussed on a relevant topic of your choice. What will I study? Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 If you’re looking to pivot to a career in artificial intelligence, this conversion course is for you. It assumes no prior exposure to computing or AI in work or study, so you’ll learn the basics before moving on to more advanced and specialist skills. You’ll learn programming, data acquisition and cleaning, data analysis and feature extraction, and machine learning – all in-demand skills among employers in this ever-growing and popular field. Why ARU? Pivot to a career in AI – no previous experience required. Gain skills that are in demand in a fast-growing field. Learn AI tools and techniques and apply them to real-world datasets. Study 100% online using our learning management system. Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . You’ll gain highly marketable applied artificial intelligence and trends prediction skills in a short amount of time, opening a wide range of career possibilities and opportunities. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. What can you do with an Applied Artificial Intelligence degree? By the end of this course, you'll be able to confidently undertake a wide range of applied computing careers including Artificial Intelligence Technologist, Data Analyst, Data Scientist, and Business Analyst for data-driven business strategies, in various domains such as healthcare, human resource, marketing, retail, e-business technologies, IT system development and design and IT project management. Using our online learning platform, you’ll explore the main principles of AI and apply them to real-world datasets. Once you’ve mastered the basics, you’ll move on to more advanced tools and techniques, such as deep learning and generative models. You’ll also choose optional modules based on your interests. You’ll complete your Master’s by conducting an end-to-end AI research and development project, based on a real-life scenario. It’s a great opportunity to demonstrate all you’ve learned on the course. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. We'll assess you in several ways including time-constrained assessments, coursework assignments, presentations and a project. Our dissertation project and module case studies assess your ability to analyse situations, identify key issues, select, synthesise and apply techniques and skills from different modules, and evaluate the appropriateness of solutions when compared to industrial practice. Your dissertation will be based on a real-world scenario. Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. These include extensive library and IT resources, and careers support through our Employability Service . After you graduate, you’ll have lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Candidates with other degrees, including foundation degrees, but with relevant work experience may also be considered. You will have normally worked for over three years in a professional environment regardless of the discipline. You will be expected to attend an interview where an assessment will be made to determine your ability to succeed at postgraduate level. If English is not your first language, you will be expected to demonstrate a certificated level of proficiency of at least IELTS 6.5 or equivalent English Language qualification as recognised by ARU. You’ll need at least 5.5 in each of the four skills - listening, speaking, reading and writing. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Thrive at the forefront of our rapidly-evolving scientific world. Gain an advanced understanding of the medical applications of bioscience, including bioinformatics, while developing the practical skills and analytical techniques needed for careers in research, healthcare or industrial settings. You'll learn in laboratories that mirror real-world laboratory environments, ensuring you’re immersed in an authentic, industry-relevant experience from day one. Accredited by the Royal Society of Biology This programme has been accredited by the Royal Society of Biology following an independent and rigorous assessment. Accredited degree programmes contain a solid academic foundation in biological knowledge and key skills, and prepare graduates to address the needs of employers. The accreditation criteria require evidence that graduates from accredited programmes meet defined sets of learning outcomes, including subject knowledge, technical ability and transferable skills. Course Director Dr Grisha Pirianov introduces our Master's courses in Advanced Biomedical Science, Applied Bioscience, Biotechnology, and Molecular Microbiology. Close full-screen gallery. Course Director Dr Grisha Pirianov introduces our Master's courses in Advanced Biomedical Science, Applied Bioscience, Biotechnology, and Molecular Microbiology. Why ARU? Study in Cambridge, one of the world's leading life sciences and biomedical innovation hubs Gain hands-on experience in specialist tissue culture and molecular laboratories, including a Category 2 lab Develop expertise in next-generation sequencing, bioinformatics and advanced molecular techniques Study on one of the UK's few Royal Society of Biology Master's-accredited bioscience programmes Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Develop the critical skills required for careers across the life sciences sector. Areas you could work in include research, environmental science, biotechnology, food and pharmaceutical industries. Opportunities include roles in laboratory research, quality assurance, scientific consultancy and technical services, with the ability to apply biological knowledge to address real-world challenges in health, industry and sustainability. What can you do with an Applied Bioscience degree? You’ll be well-prepared to progress into a wide range of careers within the biosciences sector, including academic, clinical and industrial research, clinical trials, product development, manufacturing and quality assurance. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You could choose to continue your academic career with a PhD programme at ARU, such as our MPhil/PhD Biomedical Science . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our course will enhance your knowledge, strengthen your practical and employability skills, and equip you for a successful professional career in the Cambridge industrial cluster. Dr Grisha Pirianov, Course Director Develop advanced skills in molecular cell biology, biomedical genetics, bioinformatics and specialised topics in medical diagnostics. On this course, you'll gain hands-on experience of molecular and cellular techniques used in applied bioscience, including DNA analysis, microbiology and cell culture, before conducting an independent research project that enables you to develop significant expertise in your chosen area. Throughout the course you’ll have opportunities to attend seminars or events with Cambridge’s many biotechnology companies, such as the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute, the Biomedical Campus at Addenbrooke's Hospital and the Babraham Research Institute. You'll also complete your Postgraduate Major Project (60 credits) in Year 2. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. What are Professional Experience modules? Professional Experience modules are a great way to learn more about an industry. They take place in Year 2 of your course, with each module lasting approximately 12 weeks (or one trimester). You can choose which modules to take. Options include project work on campus, and industry placements. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Applied Bioscience assessed? We use a range of assessment methods to enable both you and the university to check your progress during your studies and then to ensure that you meet the required standards when you complete the course. Although they vary, our assessment strategies are all carefully designed to challenge you so that you expand your critical and analytical thinking as well as your problem-solving skills. The assessments will enable you to demonstrate that you can synthesise existing knowledge and accumulate new knowledge, and will evidence the development of your professional practice. Some examples of assessment include poster and oral presentations, essays and portfolios of evidence. In addition, you will undertake practicals in many of the modules, developing your technical laboratory skills. Who teaches Applied Bioscience at ARU? Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Whether you're changing career or expanding your technical expertise, this conversion course in the heart of the Silicon Fen provides a practical pathway into modern data science and AI. You’ll gain hands-on experience in programming, statistics, machine learning, data visualisation, predictive analytics and generative AI through real-world datasets, and graduate with the analytical and technical skills sought by employers across healthcare, finance, business, technology and research. Why ARU? Launch your data science career – no computing or data-related degree required Study and explore career opportunities in Cambridge’s ‘Silicon Fen’, a global hub for tech innovation Build in-demand skills such as data mining, machine learning, statistical modelling and AI Apply your knowledge through hands-on projects using real-life datasets and industry-relevant projects Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers Your mentorship and belief in me have helped me learn and develop skills that I will carry with me for the rest of my career as I start my new role as a data analyst. Merin Mathew, MSc Applied Data Science (Conversion) graduate Gain in-demand skills applicable to a range of careers. This course equips you with highly marketable practical and industry-ready skills needed to thrive in today's data-driven world. You'll develop expertise in programming, data acquisition and cleaning, data visualisation, machine learning, predictive modelling, and artificial intelligence using industry-standard tools and techniques. You'll graduate well prepared for careers in data science, AI, business analytics, healthcare, finance, technology, and research. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with an Applied Data Science (Conversion) degree? Organisations and industries increasingly rely on AI and data-driven decision making to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. You might pursue careers in data science, artificial intelligence, business analytics, healthcare analytics, financial technology, cyber security, environmental modelling, smart manufacturing and research. The combination of technical, analytical and communication skills also supports you to progress into leadership roles within data-driven organisations. Where have previous Applied Data Science (Conversion) graduates worked? Previous graduates from this course have gone on to a range of roles, including: Data Scientist at NHS Arden and GEM CSU Data Analyst at Hilbrix Data Scientist at Twinkl Educational Publishing Data and Insights Manager at Adam Smith Institute AI Research & Product Development at Pathway AI Consulting Research Assistant at ARU Data Quality and Insights Analyst at National Energy System Operator Senior Data Analyst at Pay.UK How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules There are many paths to becoming a data scientist. What matters is curiosity, commitment and a willingness to learn and explore. Dr Mahdi Maktabdar Oghaz, Course Leader Develop the knowledge and practical skills needed to become a confident data scientist, whatever your previous academic background. You'll begin by building strong foundations through Analytical Techniques and Programming with Python, before progressing to Principles of Data Mining and Machine Learning, where you'll develop predictive models and extract meaningful insights from real-world data. In Applied Data Analysis and Research Methodology, you'll learn to analyse complex datasets using industry-standard tools and apply robust research methods to data-driven investigations. The course culminates in the Data Analytics Major Project, where you'll independently apply the knowledge and skills gained throughout the programme to solve a real-world problem in a domain of your choice. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Analytical Techniques (30 credits) Programming with Python (30 credits) Principles of Data Mining and Machine Learning (30 credits) Applied Data Analysis and Research Methodology (30 credits) Data Analytics Major Project (60 credits) Module details How is Applied Data Science (Conversion) assessed? We'll assess you in several ways, including time-constrained assessments, coursework assignments and a Major Project (dissertation). Our module case studies and Major Project assess your ability to analyse situations, identify key issues, select, synthesise and apply techniques and skills, and evaluate the appropriateness of solutions when compared to industrial practice. Your dissertation will be based on a real-world scenario. Who teaches Applied Data Science (Conversion) at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Professor Silvia Cirstea Deputy Head of School Dr Imran Ahmed Senior Lecturer Dr Faraz Janan Senior Lecturer Dr Mahdi Maktabdar Oghaz Senior Lecturer Facilities Enjoy a range of facilities designed to support your studies and career development. Explore the latest linguistics theories and apply them to your classroom practice. What type of teaching is best? Alastair Douglas 60 second seminar Senior Lecturer Alastair discusses the methods and techniques used by language teachers. Already have an ARU degree? You may be eligible for our Alumni Scholarship for students starting postgraduate courses. Study our MA Applied Linguistics and TESOL (Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages) in Cambridge, a city famous for language teaching, and boost your career prospects with new critical and analytical skills. On this course you’ll improve your theoretical understanding of language learning, which will help you to develop your professional teaching skills. You’ll explore the latest theories in topics such as second language acquisition and classroom theory and practice, examining different methods of analysis. Your studies will be supported throughout by our research-active and industry-experienced academics, including DELTA-qualified professionals. And if you already have the Delta or Trinity TESOL Diploma, we will give you 60 credits towards your degree. If you study this course by distance learning, you will not need to attend any face-to-face sessions. Read more Teaching times 2025-26 (subject to change for 2026-27) Trimester 1: Compulsory module: Fridays 3-5pm; optional modules: Tuesdays 2-4pm, Tuesdays 6-8pm, Wednesdays 10am-1pm Trimester 2: Compulsory modules: Tuesdays 6-8pm; optional modules: Tuesdays 2-5pm, Thursdays 12-2pm As a Masters student at ARU, we’ll help you learn to carry out your own research and how to compile and analyse quantitative and qualitative data. You’ll be able to use the critical-evaluative skills you develop on your own research project at the end of the course, as well as in your future career. Studying Applied Linguistics and TESOL will give you the chance to take part in our research seminars and high-profile conferences. We’ll also help you make valuable contacts for your future through our links to language companies such as EF, Bell, and Studio, a group for heads of language schools. Whether you study full-time in Cambridge or part-time by distance learning, this postgraduate degree opens up opportunities for you to become part of the international academic and professional English Language teaching and language-learning community. Postgraduate MSc Applied Wildlife Conservation Master practical wildlife conservation skills through applied conservation biology, fieldwork and data analysis to tackle real-world global biodiversity challenges. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. The part-time option takes 28 months (September starts), or 33 months (January starts). 2 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as MSc/MA students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students. For example if the MSc/MA course takes one year, you can expect to study over two years, though for some courses this may vary. 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 If you’re passionate about tackling global biodiversity and climate challenges, this innovative Master’s is for you. You'll develop the technical expertise and professional competencies sought by conservation employers worldwide, equipping you to champion nature in a rapidly changing world. You'll combine field-based learning with advanced technical training in biodiversity assessment methods, spatial data analysis including Geographical Information Systems (GIS), conservation communication, conservation biology research and quantitative data analysis to make a meaningful impact in conservation. Hear from our staff and students about studying Applied Wildlife Conservation at ARU. Close full-screen gallery. Hear from our staff and students about studying Applied Wildlife Conservation at ARU. Why ARU? Gain hands-on conservation experience through fieldwork, laboratory work, and real-world projects in your areas of interest Develop in-demand technical and research skills, including GIS and field survey and biodiversity assessment techniques Collaborate with conservation organisations on real-world environmental projects, Live Briefs , and research challenges Conduct your major research project with supervision from leading academics from our Centre for Ecology, Evolution and Environment Enhance your studies with an optional field skills course in France hosted by the Mediterranean Ecology Research Observatory for Practical Skills Master data handling, reporting and communication skills Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers This course gave me a wonderful opportunity to apply my lifelong love of nature to exciting worldwide contexts while challenging my academic ability. Linda Butterfield, Countryside Ranger, Lea Valley Park Prepare for an impactful career protecting wildlife and habitats. You'll graduate with skills in fieldwork, laboratory techniques (eDNA), computational ecology (GIS and R Stats), academic research, and science communication to help you secure your dream role in the conservation sector. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU, such as our PhD Biology . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with an Applied Wildlife Conservation degree? This course will prepare you for careers in areas such as conservation biology, nature conservation, ecological consultancy, conservation education, PhD research, project management, policy and governance. You may also develop a career within a non-governmental organisation (NGO), charity, zoo, private company, or government body, or in a related field such as ecotourism. Typical graduate destinations include: Wildlife conservation and management Ecological and environmental consultancy Environmental charities and NGOs Governmental organisations, local authorities and the Civil Service Project management and data analysts Conservation research and education Sustainability and environmental policy PhD study or other research work Environmental policy and governance Attending the 2025 Student Conference on Conservation Science Animal Behaviour Applications for Conservation student Afrika shares her experiences of the 2025 Student Conference on Conservation Science (SCCS) in Cambridge. Where have previous Applied Wildlife Conservation graduates worked? Graduates have furthered their careers at an array of organisations including: The Wildlife Trusts Forestry Commission Milton Keynes Parks Trust Benthic Solutions Civil Service UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology Anglian Water International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC) Mammal Society Froglife How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our MSc students are a regular source of inspiration to me. Some of the best moments of my career have been working on field trips with them. Dr Peter Brown, Associate Professor in Ecology and Conservation Develop the practical skills needed to tackle global biodiversity loss. You'll practise fieldwork, ecological survey techniques, spatial mapping, conservation genetics, research methods and science communication. You’ll apply your learning to real-world conservation challenges, specialise through optional modules, and complete an independent research project on a contemporary conservation issue. Developed with international environmental organisations, this Master's equips you with employer-valued expertise in wildlife and habitat management, data analysis and sustainable conservation, supported by field trips, specialist guest lecturers and strong links with leading conservation organisations. You'll be continually assessed through Live Briefs , group presentations, report writing, and field and lab reporting. Who teaches Applied Wildlife Conservation at ARU? Our teaching team includes internationally recognised researchers and experienced practitioners working across the fields of conservation, ecology, animal behaviour and environmental sustainability. Dr Jim Littlemore Senior Lecturer Dr Bas Boots Senior Lecturer Dr Peter Brown Associate Professor Professor Dannielle Green Professor Dr Thomas Ings Associate Professor Dr Hannah White Senior Lecturer Facilities Study in our state of the art £40m Science Centre in the heart of Cambridge. You'll have access to specialist facilities supporting animal and environmental biology and use industry-standard GIS and spatial analysis software, well stocked laboratories, field equipment and dedicated teaching spaces including our research labs. You'll learn beyond campus through residential and local field trips across East Anglia, practical training and opportunities to engage with conservation organisations. You'll also benefit from ARU's extensive library and digital learning resources and support services. Take a guided tour and meet our students . Postgraduate MArch Architecture Take the next step to becoming a registered architect of the future. Explore ethical, innovative and sustainable practice at ARU in Chelmsford. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event Start date September 2027 Location Chelmsford Award MArch Duration 2 years full-time 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 If you aspire to design innovative, sustainable spaces that contribute to a safer and more conscious world, this course is for you. Studying in our School of Architecture and Planning , you’ll develop the creative, technical and professional skills to design buildings and places that respond to environmental and social challenges. Prepare for the next stage of your architectural career, as you build the practical experience to achieve your Part 3 qualification and registration as an architect. ARB Part 2 prescribed Our Master of Architecture degree is prescribed (Part 2) by the Architects Registration Board. When you complete this course, you'll fulfil the second part of the three-part process to become a registered architect in the UK. Hear more about studying MArch Architecture at ARU. Close full-screen gallery. Hear more about studying MArch Architecture at ARU. Why ARU? Design innovative, sustainable architecture for a changing world Develop your practice in dedicated studios with expert architectural tutors Experiment with technologies including 3D fabrication, computational design, robotics and extended reality Learn from practising architects and industry specialists through weekly masterclasses Build the professional knowledge and design portfolio to progress towards architect registration Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers A thoughtfully curated programme of engaging lectures, tutorials and site visits, nurturing growth, critical thinking and my knowledge of architecture. Susan, MArch Part 2 graduate Advance your journey towards becoming a registered architect with ARU's Master of Architecture (MArch). Accredited as ARB Part 2, this course prepares you for the final stage of professional qualification in the UK. You’ll graduate with the advanced design, technical and professional skills to progress towards Part 3 and a rewarding career in architectural practice, urban design and the wider built environment. What can you do with an Architecture degree? You could work in any architectural practice in the UK and abroad, create a start-up collective, work as a computational designer or product designer, work with planning authorities, or focus on interior and landscape design. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU, such as our PhD Engineering and the Built Environment . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Advance your architectural career by combining creative design, technological innovation, sustainability and professional expertise in a dynamic studio environment. Marco Vanucci, Course Director Develop the knowledge, creativity and professional skills to become a conscientious architectural practitioner. Through studio-based learning, you’ll explore a range of technical and creative-practical topics while working with real clients, gaining hands-on experience and insights into every stage of a typical architectural project. Alongside design practice, you'll examine issues shaping the profession, including sustainability, ethics and the role of architecture in society. You'll complete the course with a substantial research project, investigating a topic that reflects your interests and career ambitions. Architecture graduate Susan reflects on her university journey at ARU, and offers advice for future students. Learn to design sustainable architecture for a changing world. Learn to design sustainable architecture for a changing world. Give your imagination free rein and master the advanced skills to create original pieces of work. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Design Studio 1 Technology Mediated Design (30 credits) Tools, Techniques, Materials and Media (15 credits) Design Studio 2 Practice Mediated Design (15 credits) Ethical and Reflective Practice (15 credits) Transdisciplinary Research Methods (15 credits) Dissertation - Design Manifesto (30 credits) Into ARU Year 2 Studio 3.1 Integrated Architectural Design Thesis (30 credits) Environmental Consciousness and Climate Literacy (15 credits) The Architect in Practice (15 credits) Studio 3.2 Integrated Architectural Design Thesis (60 credits) Module details How is Architecture assessed? Assessment is progressive, allowing you to build on previously acquired knowledge and skills, with feedback and feedforward used to effectively support and facilitate such development. We provide tutorials, interim crits, final reviews, assessment literacy, and online resources designed to support you in attaining relevant skills to undertake the assessments. Assessment methods include: design projects, portfolio assessment, coursework, case study reports, computer-based exercises, individual and group presentations, timed assignments, written dissertation and essays to promote an understanding of good practice is supporting claims with evidence and referencing, role-play tasks in all design modules’ live briefs to promote experience and reflective skills. Who teaches MArch Architecture at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. Richard Gatti Senior Lecturer Practitioner Dr Giacomo Damiani Senior Lecturer Facilities You’ll be based in our School of Architecture and Planning , with use of: model-making studios industry-standard software for computer-aided design work construction and surveying equipment a fully equipped workshop with cutting-edge digital fabrication machinery and skilled staff specialist 3D printers that are available to all students. All our architecture students can take part in team activities such as designing and building structures on campus. Being just 35 minutes from London by train allows for numerous short study and site visits and workshops. Take a guided tour and meet our students .
