Postgraduate MSc Veterinary Physiotherapy Develop advanced veterinary physiotherapy skills to optimise performance, support rehabilitation, and improve animal welfare. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Book on a postgraduate open event Start date September 2027 Location Writtle Award MSc Duration 3 years part-time 1st in the region for postgraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: Graduate Outcomes Survey 2026 Advance your expertise in veterinary physiotherapy with this flexible, part-time MSc designed for graduates and animal health professionals. Delivered over three years through blended learning and residential weekends, you'll develop advanced clinical reasoning, rehabilitation and therapeutic skills for horses and dogs. You'll also gain valuable research, professional and business expertise, preparing you for a successful career in veterinary physiotherapy and animal rehabilitation. RAMP and AHPR This course is recognised by the Register of Animal Musculoskeletal Practitioners (RAMP), and pending accreditation by the Animal Health Professions’ Register (AHPR). It meets industry-recognised professional standards and competencies and prepares you to pursue professional registration and career opportunities in the animal rehabilitation sector. Why ARU? Study the anatomy and biomechanics of horses and dogs Learn through flexible blended delivery and residential practical weekends Develop hands-on skills in equine and canine rehabilitation Access specialist facilities, including commercial canine clinics Build confidence through real-world case studies and clinical placements Complete your MSc alongside your existing professional commitments Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers [This is] an outstanding course with substantial hands-on clinic time led by engaging lecturers. Drawing from their own veterinary physiotherapy practices, they add incredible depth to a rewarding course that means I now get to do my dream job! Claire Bidwell, MSc Veterinary Physiotherapy graduate Turn your passion for animal health and rehabilitation into a rewarding career. This MSc will equip you with advanced clinical, research and professional skills valued across the animal health, rehabilitation and welfare sectors. You might progress into veterinary physiotherapy practice, animal rehabilitation, clinical consultancy, education, research, product development, animal welfare organisations and related industries. The course also develops the business and communication skills needed to establish an independent practice or expand an existing professional role. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to continue your academic career and join a research programme at ARU. Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and save £400 on your fees. What can you do with a Veterinary Physiotherapy degree? Graduates can pursue a range of careers across animal health, rehabilitation and welfare. Many work as veterinary physiotherapists supporting the assessment, treatment and rehabilitation of horses and dogs, either independently or as part of multidisciplinary teams. The advanced clinical, research and professional skills developed on this course can also support careers in animal rehabilitation centres, education and training, research, consultancy, animal welfare organisations, product development and the wider animal health sector. The course is also well suited to professionals looking to enhance their existing roles or develop specialist expertise. Where have previous Veterinary Physiotherapy graduates worked? Our graduates have gone on to establish successful veterinary physiotherapy businesses, join multidisciplinary veterinary and rehabilitation practices, and work within the wider animal health sector. Career destinations include: veterinary physiotherapy and rehabilitation clinics veterinary practices hydrotherapy centres equine performance and rehabilitation facilities animal welfare organisations education and training research, consultancy, and product development technical and sales support insurance services clinical advisory roles. The advanced clinical, communication and business skills developed throughout the course will prepare you for a wide range of opportunities across the animal health and rehabilitation industries. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning which may include industry-led projects, placements or Professional Experience modules . Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our students arrive from all sorts of pathways – seeing how far they develop is incredibly rewarding. Hope Jameson, Senior Lecturer Combine advanced scientific knowledge with practical clinical skills. You'll explore comparative anatomy, biomechanics, pathology and rehabilitation, developing the knowledge needed to assess and treat a range of equine and canine conditions. Throughout the course, you'll strengthen your clinical reasoning, communication and professional practice skills, while considering ethical, legal and sustainability issues within animal healthcare. Practical training, clinical experiences and case-based learning will help you apply theory to real-world situations. In your final year, you'll complete an independent research project, investigating a topic relevant to veterinary physiotherapy and animal rehabilitation. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Animal Structure, Function and Pathology (45 credits) Academic and Professional Development for Future Success (15 credits) Year 2 Advancing Clinical Skills and Professional Development (30 credits) Advanced Therapy, Manual and Electrophysical Agents and Exercise Prescription (30 credits) Year 3 Major Project (60 credits) Module details What are the teaching times? This course is designed to fit around professional and personal commitments, with most face-to-face teaching taking place during residential weekends at our Writtle campus. Teaching days typically run from 9am to 5pm and include a mix of lectures, workshops and practical sessions. Alongside on-campus teaching, you'll engage with online learning materials and independent study throughout the programme. In Year 1, you'll attend approximately 12 teaching and assessment weekends, while Year 2 includes around 18 weekends, incorporating practical training and internal clinical placement days. How do placements work? Clinical experience is integrated throughout the course, allowing you to apply your learning in real-world settings while developing practical skills and professional confidence. You'll gain experience through internal placement opportunities, including access to our commercial canine clinics and specialist equine facilities. You'll also have opportunities to observe and work alongside practising clinicians, engaging with real cases and rehabilitation programmes. External visits and practical experiences further enhance your understanding of professional practice, helping you develop the clinical reasoning and hands-on skills required for a career in veterinary physiotherapy. How is Veterinary Physiotherapy assessed? Assessment methods are designed to reflect the knowledge, practical skills and professional competencies required in veterinary physiotherapy practice. You'll complete a variety of assessments throughout the course, including case studies, scientific reports, presentations, clinical portfolios, practical examinations, research evaluations and online activities. Practical skills are assessed through observed structured clinical examinations (OSCEs), while your final year culminates in an independent research project focused on a topic relevant to veterinary physiotherapy and animal rehabilitation. This diverse approach allows you to demonstrate both theoretical understanding and practical expertise while developing skills valued by employers and professional bodies. English language requirements If English is not your first language, you'll need to make sure you meet our English language requirements for postgraduate courses . Check the section ' English language requirements ' for IELTS requirements. Interviews We conduct interviews for our MSc Veterinary Physiotherapy course. If invited to interview, you can sign up for a timeslot through our Applicant Portal (we'll send you details of how to access the Portal). All interviews will be held online, and relevant links will be shared closer to the interview date. You'll be required to submit any outstanding application material ahead of the interview. This includes copies of all qualifications, letters provided from referees, evidence of required equine and canine practical placements to include 50 hours in equine and 50 hours in canine settings. If you cannot provide evidence of completed placements, please provide evidence of secured, upcoming placements that will fulfil these requirements. You will also be required to provide video evidence of your equine handling skills, following the instructions below. This video should be under ten minutes. You will need to: 1) Introduce yourself to the camera wearing the appropriate PPE, please ensure we can see your face before you proceed to the following tasks. 2) Enter safely a stable where a horse is waiting for you. 3) Secure the horse using the head collar. 4) Put an adequate bridle on the horse safely. 5) Pick the left hind and clean the hoof. 6) Remove the equipment. 7) Exit the stable. The video must not be edited. Running commentaries are not necessary. Please send this video to [email protected] and ensure your student ID number is included in the email. The video should reach us by no later than one week before your selected interview date. Please enable JavaScript for "Fees Information" section to function. Fees and funding UK students £15,940 UK students starting 2027/28 (total cost) Fees for our MSc Veterinary Physiotherapy vary by year. For UK students starting in 2027-28 the fees are £6,380 in Year 1, £6,380 in Year 2, and £3,180 in Year 3. Fees are payable upfront, in full or in instalments, but there's no need to pay until you've accepted an offer to study with us. Find out more about paying your fees and about postgraduate loans and funding . Additional course costs For this course, you'll need access to a laptop and a reliable internet connection. Practical course equipment/uniform To take part in practical activities safely and comfortably, you’ll need a riding hat or skull cap that meets current BETA safety standards, riding gloves and sturdy yard boots, long or short. Clothing should be smart and practical, such as dark trousers, waterproofs, or plain jeans (no rips or embellishments). A warm, waterproof outdoor coat (no hood) is also important, plus a digital camera or phone can come in handy for recording your practical work. A lab coat will also be needed for practical sessions in the laboratory. Estimated: £15–£25 Estimated cost for basic yard wear and equipment: £150–£250. During canine hydrotherapy sessions we recommend students to have their own set of waders to ensure comfort and size. Estimated £27-45. Re-take fees for practical exams (OSPEs) may also be incurred. The fee is currently £20 each time. The following additional costs apply in your second year In your second year, you will need to arrange individual insurance as you’ll be treating patients. This will cover you during clinical placements. It is compulsory in order to practice and treat patients. We recommend that you use Balens which is £23.18 (2025). In your second year, you will be working alongside clients and members of the public and will need to dress professionally. The following equipment and uniform are a requirement. Equine: stool for equine practicals (Estimated: £10-20) Canine: wetsuit or waders for hydrotherapy (Estimated: £25-50) Indoor shoes: black trainers (no coloured logos) or boots (Estimated £10-60) T-shirt or long sleeve top (black or navy) (Estimated: £4-20) Fleece (black or navy) (Estimated: £15-50) Trousers: black jeggings or jeans; no blue rinse jeans, rips or embellishments (Estimated: £10-30) Black or brown boots for the yard (Estimated: £25-£150) All clothing must be free of large motifs or branding. Any logos should be small and discreet. No sleeveless tops, or shorts or hoodies are allowed. Source: GOS 2026 Using hands-on practical experiences, our Accounting and Finance degree will equip you with the industry skills to enter the fields of accounting, finance and broader business. Whether it’s practicing in the Bloomberg Financial Markets Labs in Cambridge or Chelmsford, or by taking part in our dedicated Accounting and Finance Student Conference in Peterborough, immersing yourself in live projects with businesses, or working on Xero™ accounting software, you'll develop a deep understanding of the tools you need to launch your career. Alongside these practical opportunities, you'll learn all about the ever-changing world of business to enhance your professional development and employability. Accreditation and Partnerships Our Accounting and Finance degree is accredited by ACCA, CIMA, CIPFA and ICAEW. You’ll be exempted from the nine Applied Knowledge and Skills papers of the ACCA qualification, four of the 15 exams of the ICAEW's ACA qualification, eight of the 16 exams of the CIMA qualification, and six of the 12 exams of the CIPFA qualification. CISI Partner University - you'll have the opportunity to study and sit CISI exams plus be a member of CISI. Accounting, Economics and Finance students sharing what their course is actually like — in their own words. Close full-screen gallery. Accounting, Economics and Finance students sharing what their course is actually like — in their own words. Why ARU? Develop expertise in accounting, finance and commercial decision-making Learn to interpret financial data to support organisational success Build practical analytical skills valued across the finance sector Explore contemporary issues including financial technology and global markets Prepare for careers in accounting, banking, auditing and financial management Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers I loved how practical and career-focused the course was. It helped me understand real-world financial applications, which made my transition into the corporate world much smoother. Cirillo Chirullo, ARU graduate and Tax Junior Our Accounting and Finance degree course will set you up with all the theoretical and practical knowledge you need to work in finance or as an accountant after you graduate. Whether it’s in our Bloomberg Financial Markets Lab in Chelmsford and Cambridge, working on leading FinTech applications in Peterborough, out on placement or through a live project, you’ll get the chance to put what you learn to the test throughout your course and gain valuable experience. Graduation doesn’t need to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our renowned MSc Accounting and Finance or MSc Finance and Financial Technologies . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship , and get 20% off your fees. What can you do with an Accounting and Finance degree? This degree prepares you for a multitude of careers, including finance, banking, insurance and the charity sector. You could go on to become a practicing accountant or opt for a wide range of careers in the business sector. You may find yourself working in a global corporation, a small to medium-sized enterprise (SME) or even for yourself – it’s not unusual for company CEOs to come from an accounting or finance background. From accounting student to business founder Accounting and Finance graduate Adrian has combined his skills in finance, business strategy and marketing to establish his own business. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Studying accounting and finance is about understanding the language of business. It equips you with the analytical skills to make sound financial decisions. Laura Muncey, Deputy Head of School You’ll start by developing a broad understanding of, and fundamental skills in financial analysis and management, global and international approaches, business law, and digital and marketing. In years 2 and 3, you’ll deepen your knowledge and skills in financial management and reporting, encompassing performance management, UK taxation, governance and auditing, and capital markets and investment. In Year 3, you’ll also complete a Major Project. As part of an interdisciplinary team, you’ll use everything you’ve learned on the course to address a current issue in business, and present your findings. A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. What happens on a placement year? Your placement year is a chance to put everything you’ve learnt in Years 1 and 2 into practice. Spend typically 9-12 months working for an organisation, developing your skills and gaining valuable work experience. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Accounting and Finance assessed? We'll assess your work in a number of ways including exams, coursework, essays and activity-based assignments. Expect, for example, problem-solving activities, consultancy projects, presentations, computer-based exams, a trading simulation portfolio, and group or individual reports. You'll also be able to access support materials through our learning management system, Canvas. Who teaches Accounting and Finance at ARU Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course. The placement year fee is: £1,700 (2026-27) You will be responsible for covering the cost of travelling to your placement during your placement year. This cost could vary significantly depending on where your placement is located, where you live during your course and how you travel. Living costs Living at university We understand that affordability is an important issue when you’re thinking about studying at university. The overall cost of university can vary depending on where you’re studying and which course you’re taking. Costs may also be lower if you're living at home. However, some of the main costs you’ll want to think about include: accommodation bills internet, mobile phone and calls travel food and drink socialising and going out study materials. Most full-time UK students can apply for a Maintenance Loan to help cover living costs. More about maintenance loans . We also have a range of offers to help with the cost of living . Our Money Advice Service is on hand if you’d like to chat about living costs, budgets and managing your money. You can also find out more about student finance at one of our Open Days . Bursaries, scholarships and part-time work We offer a range of scholarships and bursaries for UK and international students , which provide extra financial support while you’re at university. If you're eligible for a scholarship, you'll generally receive it automatically – there's no need to apply. Our campus employment bureau, ARU Temps , can help you find part-time work that fits around your studies (including any time you may spend on placements). It's a great chance to enhance your CV and boost your income while you study. Source: NSS 2026 Grow into a confident and versatile performer. Focus on fundamental acting skills, voice and movement, screen acting, and how to rehearse for a full production. Work with experienced directors, experiment with physical theatre, learn about new performance technologies, and extend your experience with screen acting and classical text. In your final year, our Immersive Performance module and Showcase will allow you to demonstrate your high-level skills in acting. Why ARU? Train in professional-standard facilities including our 260-seater Mumford Theatre Gain experience with new technologies and alternative platforms to become a dynamic and responsive actor Develop your technical and production skills in specialist facilities for recorded and live performance Graduate with a professional CV, headshots and showreel Collaborate with other creative students, experienced tutors, community partners and industry professionals Get involved with Cambridge's many acting troupes and events Designed for creative life Our Creative Quarter brings together studios, workshops, performance and exhibition spaces. Be part of a community built around making, experimentation and innovation, while developing your practical skills and portfolio, and connecting with industry. Careers We've done different shows with different instructors, and they all have different methods to how they direct. I think that's invaluable. Trey Augustus, BA (Hons) Acting Throughout your degree, you’ll develop creativity and technical competence in a range of acting media, including both live and recorded performance. You’ll develop transferable skills such as research, teamwork, communication, problem solving, and resourcefulness – invaluable in all areas of the creative industries as well as other sectors. You’ll also have opportunities to take part in collaborative work, like our HMS Belfast project with the Imperial War Museum, commemorating D-Day, and 60 Second Shakespeare with the Globe theatre, London. What can you do with an Acting degree? By the time you graduate, you’ll have built up a professional portfolio of your acting projects, which will act as an enhanced CV for you to present to agents, employers and clients – whether you want to act in live performance, on screen, or even be a voice or motion-capture artist for games and other new media. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules There are many different ways of using acting skills in a whole variety of media. So our aim is to prepare students for that multi-platform world. David Jackson, Course Director In your first year, you’ll be introduced to effective working methodologies in both performance and production, producing a studio-based collaborative live performance, developing core physical and vocal skills and being introduced to acting for the camera. In your second year, you’ll work with an experienced theatre director as a member of a production company, creating a theatre piece for live performance. Finally, our Immersive Performance module, Showcase and Major Project will allow you to demonstrate your high-level skills in acting and focus specifically on your employability. Year 1 Studio Performance Voice and Movement Introduction to Screen Acting Fundamentals for Acting Into ARU Year 2 Ruskin Module (15 credits) Performance Project Physical Theatre Performance Technologies Performing Shakespeare Storytelling on Screen: Collaborative Project Directing and Choreography * Year 3 Immersive Performance Showcase Creative Industries Major Project Module details With placement You can choose to take an optional placement year as part of this course. Placements typically happen in Year 3, and your course will take four years overall. Find out more about placement years . Placement year Work Placement - Cambridge School of Creative Industries Module details With foundation year To prepare you for university study, you can take a foundation year at the start of this course. Find out more about foundation years . Year 1 Foundation in Humanities, English, Media, Social Sciences and Education Module details What happens on a foundation year? A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. What happens on a placement year? Your placement year is a chance to put everything you’ve learnt in Years 1 and 2 into practice. Spend typically 9-12 months working for an organisation, developing your skills and gaining valuable work experience. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Acting assessed? You’ll show your progress through a variety of methods that reflect the skills and knowledge you’ll need as both a practitioner and critic, able to both make work and analyse it. These will test your ability, technique, creativity and production skills, and involve both collaborative practice and individual work. They include: live or mediated performance; process in creating performance (e.g rehearsals, collaborative skills, and professional conduct); rationales for performance; technical production work; critical reflection; essays; portfolios; design plans (e.g. lighting, sound, costume, shooting scripts for video); reviews; practical demonstrations; workshop facilitation; and oral presentations / examinations. Living costs Living at university We understand that affordability is an important issue when you’re thinking about studying at university. The overall cost of university can vary depending on where you’re studying and which course you’re taking. Costs may also be lower if you're living at home. However, some of the main costs you’ll want to think about include: accommodation bills internet, mobile phone and calls travel food and drink socialising and going out study materials. Most full-time UK students can apply for a Maintenance Loan to help cover living costs. More about maintenance loans . We also have a range of offers to help with the cost of living . Our Money Advice Service is on hand if you’d like to chat about living costs, budgets and managing your money. You can also find out more about student finance at one of our Open Days . Bursaries, scholarships and part-time work We offer a range of scholarships and bursaries for UK and international students , which provide extra financial support while you’re at university. If you're eligible for a scholarship, you'll generally receive it automatically – there's no need to apply. Our campus employment bureau, ARU Temps , can help you find part-time work that fits around your studies (including any time you may spend on placements). Source: GOS 2026 Our course takes a progressive, future-focused approach to addressing the evolving needs of agriculture today. You'll explore how the industry must adapt to climate change, shifting policies and global food demands by integrating sustainable practices, innovation and systems thinking. Through real-world learning on our extensive working farm, you’ll examine the full agri-food supply chain, emerging technologies and the role of agriculture in delivering environmental and social value, preparing you to shape the future of a resilient, responsible industry. Learn more about studying Agriculture at ARU. Close full-screen gallery. Learn more about studying Agriculture at ARU. Why ARU? Immerse yourself in authentic, enquiry-led learning using our 150-hectare estate and working mixed farm Discover how technology, innovation and data can create sustainable farming systems that address climate change while ensuring food security Accelerate your career through placements, industry collaborations and a strong alumni network across agribusinesses Collaborate on real-world challenges through live briefs, research projects and industry events to shape tomorrow’s food systems Gain confidence and leadership skills from multidisciplinary experts to drive change in global agriculture Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers My experience at Writtle has opened me up to realise there are a lot more jobs than working on a farm in agriculture, such as agronomy and land agency. Emily Keeble, BSc (Hons) Agriculture As a BSc (Hons) Agriculture graduate, you'll have a sound understanding of arable and livestock farming, as well as the wider environment in which production takes place. You’ll graduate equipped with real-life practical skills, industry insight and the ability to apply sustainable and innovative solutions, preparing you to drive innovation, influence policy and contribute to the future of food security and environmental stewardship in the UK and globally. What can you do with an Agriculture degree? You can pursue diverse career roles across the entire food supply chain as well as farm management, sustainability leadership, agricultural consulting, technology development, supply chain management and food science. Opportunities also exist in ESG and data analytics, agronomy, policy analysis, research science and precision agriculture, driving innovation and promoting sustainable practices in agriculture. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our MBA Agribusiness or MSc Crop Production . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. Where have other Agriculture graduates worked? Previous graduates have gone onto a variety of job roles, including: Agricultural Consultant Agronomist Animal Nutritionist Crop Specialist Estate Manager Farm Manager Land Agent Nutrition Company Sales Representative Postgraduate Qualification or Research Rural Practice Surveyor Soil Scientist Reggie Deakin – Assistant Farm Manager at 21 After graduating with a degree in Agriculture from ARU Writtle, Reggie Deakin stepped into a senior role at Wigborough Wick Farm in Essex. He now manages a 300-cow dairy herd and is leading improvements in livestock systems. “Being trusted with this responsibility straight out of university means a lot,” says Reggie, who’s already making a difference in cow welfare and farm efficiency. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules From soil to strawberries, spring wheat to sheep, and everything in between, students explore a diverse range of topics that are essential for shaping the future of farming and addressing the challenges of tomorrow's food systems. Harriet Wishart, Lecturer Study scientific, economic and managerial principles to support sustainable agriculture. You'll focus on real-world applications, using our own commercial farm and local businesses for hands-on learning. Your modules will cover areas such as ecosystems, agri-tech, net zero farming, animal welfare and agribusiness. You’ll explore supply chains, food systems and policy through both practical and theoretical approaches. In the final year, you’ll undertake a major research project, developing skills for your future career in agriculture. What will I study? CertHE UK students have the option to study Year 1 of this course, either for one year full-time or two years part-time, to achieve a CertHE. You can also choose to combine a foundation year with the CertHE. Contact us to discuss what you can do, or choose your preferred option when you apply. What happens on a foundation year? A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. What happens on a placement year? Your placement year is a chance to put everything you’ve learnt in Years 1 and 2 into practice. Spend typically 9-12 months working for an organisation, developing your skills and gaining valuable work experience. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is this course assessed? We'll assess your progress in a number of ways including reports, examinations, presentations – both individually and in small groups, essays and technical reports, assessed roundtable discussions, case studies, experimental work and laboratory reports, poster presentations, debates, and your dissertation. Living costs Living at university We understand that affordability is an important issue when you’re thinking about studying at university. The overall cost of university can vary depending on where you’re studying and which course you’re taking. Costs may also be lower if you're living at home. However, some of the main costs you’ll want to think about include: accommodation bills internet, mobile phone and calls travel food and drink socialising and going out study materials. Most full-time UK students can apply for a Maintenance Loan to help cover living costs. More about maintenance loans . We also have a range of offers to help with the cost of living . Our Money Advice Service is on hand if you’d like to chat about living costs, budgets and managing your money. You can also find out more about student finance at one of our Open Days . Bursaries, scholarships and part-time work We offer a range of scholarships and bursaries for UK and international students , which provide extra financial support while you’re at university. If you're eligible for a scholarship, you'll generally receive it automatically – there's no need to apply. Our campus employment bureau, ARU Temps , can help you find part-time work that fits around your studies (including any time you may spend on placements). It's a great chance to enhance your CV and boost your income while you study. Undergraduate BSc (Hons) Agriculture with Business Drive the future of sustainable agriculture and agri-business and tackle global challenges head on with our innovative business degree. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Come to an Open Day BSc (Hons) With placement BSc (Hons) Start date September 2027 Location Writtle UCAS course code D403 Duration 3 years With placement Start date September 2027 Location Writtle UCAS course code D407 Duration 4 years with placement 1st in the region for undergraduates progressing into senior roles. Source: GOS 2026 Our BSc (Hons) Agriculture with Business degree offers a forward-thinking, holistic approach that prepares you to lead in the evolving agri-business world by combining practical science with commercial problem-solving. You’ll explore global challenges like food security, climate change and sustainability, gaining hands-on experience on our working farm, through real-world case studies and an embedded placement year. With expert teaching and industry connections, you’ll be ready for diverse and exciting careers in the agricultural business sector. Why ARU? Immerse yourself in authentic, enquiry-led learning using our 150-hectare estate and working mixed farm Discover how technology, innovation and data can create sustainable farming systems that address climate change while ensuring food security Boost your employability with an optional industry placement year between Levels 5 and 6 Collaborate on real-world challenges through live briefs, research projects and industry events to shape tomorrow’s food systems Gain confidence and leadership skills from multidisciplinary experts to drive change in global agriculture Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers My experience at Writtle has opened me up to realise there are a lot more jobs than working on a farm in agriculture, such as agronomy and land agency. Emily Keeble, BSc (Hons) Agriculture Studying this course equips you with the skills and knowledge to thrive in the UK’s £28.2 billion food and beverage sector. You'll develop expertise in agri-business management, supply chains, sustainability and consumer trends, alongside critical thinking, problem-solving and commercial awareness. These in-demand skills prepare you for roles in food quality, planning, buying, trading, and graduate schemes, while also giving you the confidence to explore business start-up opportunities. What can you do with an Agriculture with Business degree? This degree prepares you for diverse careers across the agri-food and rural business sectors. You could pursue roles in farm management, food quality, supply chain coordination, fresh produce trading or join graduate schemes in leading agri-food companies. The degree also opens doors to consultancy, sustainability roles, rural development or launching your own agri-business venture. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our MBA Agribusiness . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. Where have other Agriculture with Business graduates worked? Previous graduates have gone onto a variety of job roles, including: Farm Business Manager Agricultural Consultant Supply Chain Manager (Agri-Food) Fresh Produce Buyer or Trader Food Quality and Safety Coordinator Agri-Business Development Executive How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules From soil to strawberries, spring wheat to sheep, and everything in between, students explore a diverse range of topics that are essential for shaping the future of farming and addressing the challenges of tomorrow's food systems. Harriet Wishart, Lecturer Throughout your degree, you’ll be taught by a multi-disciplinary team with real-world industry experience. From year one, you’ll dive into modules like ecosystems, biological processes and global business, building a strong foundation in both science and strategy. In year two, you’ll explore sustainable farming, animal production, fresh produce and consumer trends through workshops, case studies, and team projects. You can then apply your learning on an optional industry placement year, and in your final year you’ll undertake a major research project, developing skills for your future career in agriculture. Undergraduate BSc (Hons) Animal Management (Zoo and Wildlife Conservation) Turn your passion for zoo animals and wildlife conservation into a career protecting our animals and their ecosystems. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Facilities Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Come to an Open Day BSc (Hons) With foundation year CertHE Part-time BSc (Hons) Start date September 2027 Location Writtle UCAS course code D305 Duration 3 years With foundation year Start date September 2027 Location Writtle UCAS course code DF05 Duration 4 years with foundation CertHE UK students have the option to study Year 1 of this course, either for one year full-time or two years part-time, to achieve a CertHE. You can also choose to combine a foundation year with the CertHE. Contact us to discuss what you can do, or choose your preferred option when you apply. Part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as BSc/BA (Hons) students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students; for example if the BSc/BA (Hons) course takes three years, you can expect to study over six years, though for some courses the part-time length may differ. 1st in the region for graduates progressing into senior roles. Source: GOS 2026 If you’re passionate about protecting wildlife and working with exotic species, our BSc (Hons) Animal Management (Zoo and Wildlife Conservation) degree prepares you for a rewarding career in zoos, conservation and animal welfare. By combining hands-on experience with animals and academic study in health, nutrition, behaviour and sustainability, you’ll gain the practical skills and industry insight through field trips and expert-led learning, equipping you to make a real impact in the animal industry. Find out more about studying Animal Management at ARU in this short video. Close full-screen gallery. Find out more about studying Animal Management at ARU in this short video. Why ARU? Develop expertise in surveying a wide variety of zoo and wildlife species Meet industry experts and build valuable professional connections through guest lectures and field trips Access strong links with leading zoos, wildlife trusts and conservation Combine practical skills with academic knowledge to make a real impact in animal welfare and conservation Careers Studying this course at ARU Writtle has opened my eyes to real-world conservation challenges, helping me gain the skills, knowledge, and confidence to pursue a career that makes a meaningful difference to animals’ lives. Kelly Laxton, BSc (Hons) Animal Management (Zoo and Wildlife Conservation) By the time you graduate, you’ll have the confidence and skills to step straight into the animal industry. You’ll know how to care for a wide range of species, understand health, nutrition and behaviour, and apply conservation strategies that make a real impact. Plus, with research, communication and networking skills under your belt, plus strong links to zoos and wildlife organisations, you’ll be ready for roles in zookeeping, conservation, education and beyond. What can you do with an Animal Management (Zoo and Wildlife Conservation) degree? After graduating, you’ll be ready for a wide range of roles in the animal sector. Whether you see yourself working hands-on in zoos, supporting wildlife conservation projects, managing animal welfare programmes, or inspiring others through education and research, this degree gives you the practical skills and industry insight to succeed. You’ll also benefit from our strong links with zoos, wildlife trusts and conservation organisations to kick-start your career. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our MSc Animal Welfare and Conservation or MSc Conservation Education and Engagement . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. Where have other Animal Management (Zoo and Wildlife Conservation) graduates worked? Previous graduates have gone onto a variety of job roles, including: zoo keeping zoo nutrition zoo and wildlife education. You could also consider roles in related fields, with other graduates finding success working in animal nutrition, animal welfare officer roles and animal research technician roles. You might also progress to vet school. From ARU to Wildlife Experience Presenter "Everything I do in my role now is rooted in what I learned at ARU Writtle. The course gave me a strong foundation in animal welfare, behaviour, and management, as well as the communication skills to share that knowledge effectively." How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Our students gain professional practical skills in wildlife surveying and the opportunity to learn from experts at leading zoos. Dr Jonathan Amory, Associate Professor You’ll begin by exploring the fundamentals of animal management, covering biology, ethics and essential practical and professional skills. In years two and three, you’ll build on your knowledge of these core topics by focusing on behaviour, breeding and animal health in relation to zoo animals and wildlife. Finally, you’ll complete an independent research project on a topic of your choice. It’s a great opportunity to dive deeper into an area that interests you in more depth while demonstrating everything you’ve learned. What will I study? You can also choose to combine a foundation year with the CertHE. Contact us to discuss what you can do, or choose your preferred option when you apply. Part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as BSc/BA (Hons) students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students; for example if the BSc/BA (Hons) course takes three years, you can expect to study over six years, though for some courses the part-time length may differ. What happens on a foundation year? A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. How is Animal Management (Zoo and Wildlife Conservation) assessed? We'll assess your progress in a number of ways including practical assessments with companion and zoo animals, farm livestock and horses, examinations – both multiple choice and essay questions, presentations – both individually and in small groups, essays and technical reports, assessed seminars, case studies, experimental work and laboratory reports, poster presentations, debates, and your dissertation. What equipment will I need? You’ll need a laptop, along with standard safety equipment for outdoor work. This includes steel toe-capped boots or wellingtons, long-sleeved overalls and a waterproof jacket and trousers. The estimated cost is between £100 and £250. You’ll also need notebook and paper for note taking, pens, pencils folders and a scientific calculator. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in optional animal and conservation trips, both locally and overseas. Please note that these trips are self-funded at your own expense. Undergraduate BSc (Hons) Animal Science Develop expertise in animal biology, health, nutrition, behaviour and welfare through hands-on practice and cutting-edge scientific learning. Source: GOS 2026 Our BSc (Hons) Animal Science degree blends pure and applied science with hands-on animal management. You’ll explore animal biology, behaviour, health, genetics, nutrition and welfare while developing strong practical and communication skills. Through laboratory work, animal handling sessions, industry links and interactions with industry professionals, you’ll apply scientific principles to real-world contexts, preparing you for diverse animal-related careers or postgraduate study. Find out more about studying Animal Science at ARU in this short video. Close full-screen gallery. Find out more about studying Animal Science at ARU in this short video. Why ARU? Gain a strong scientific foundation through a blend of pure and applied animal sciences Develop practical competence with a wide range of domesticated and captive species Learn from industry-recognised experts and guest speakers from leading animal organisations Benefit from hands-on animal handling sessions and dedicated laboratory facilities Apply your knowledge through field visits and real-world industry engagement Graduate equipped for careers in welfare, research, farming, veterinary support or progress onto further education Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers The BSc (Hons) Animal Science degree at Writtle was an incredible opportunity to gain invaluable skills and knowledge relating to animal health, welfare and behaviour, from lecturers that truly engage you and help you throughout your career. Isabelle Ormes, BSc (Hons) Animal Science This course will equip you with the strong scientific, practical and research skills valued by employers across the animal industry. You’ll gain experience with a range of species, develop confident lab and field competencies, and build industry connections through field visits and guest speakers. What can you do with a Animal Science degree? With a BSc (Hons) Animal Science, you can pursue a wide range of roles across the animal and biological industries. Graduates commonly move into careers in animal welfare, behaviour, nutrition, research, farming and livestock management, captive-animal collections and veterinary support. The degree also provides a strong foundation for postgraduate study, including specialised master’s programmes or pathways into research and veterinary-related fields. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our MSc Animal Welfare and Conservation or MSc Conservation Education and Engagement . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. Where have other Animal Science graduates worked? Graduates from BSc (Hons) Animal Science progress into a wide range of job roles, including: Animal nutrition Pet food manufacturing Veterinary pharmaceutical and equipment supply Education Animal welfare Captive animal environments (e.g. RSPCA, SSPCA, rescue centres) Quarantine management Animal health inspection (e.g. DEFRA) Independent wildlife agencies (e.g. RSPB, Scottish Natural Heritage, Natural England) You might also progress to vet school. How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules From the basics of animal biology to specialist topics such as behaviour and nutrition, our course equips you with the skills, knowledge and experience to understand, care for, and sustainably improve the lives of animals. Dr Nnenna Ugwu, Lecturer and Course Director The course begins by covering the core principals of biology, ethics, behaviour, nutrition, genetics, health and essential practical and professional skills. In your second and third year, you’ll deepen this knowledge and have the opportunity to specialise in areas that interest you, such as bioveterinary science or farm livestock. In your final year, you’ll complete a capstone project, conducting research a topic of your choice, applying your skills in data analysis, research and communication, while demonstrating your expertise across animal science and welfare. You can also choose to combine a foundation year with the CertHE. Contact us to discuss what you can do, or choose your preferred option when you apply. 6 years part-time It's possible to study this course part-time. You'll take the same modules as BSc/BA (Hons) students, but sometimes in a different order or in different years. As a part-time student you'll typically study for twice as long as full-time students; for example if the BSc/BA (Hons) course takes three years, you can expect to study over six years, though for some courses the part-time length may differ. What happens on a foundation year? A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. How is Animal Science assessed? We will assess your progress in a number of ways. This includes practical assessments with companion and zoo animals, farm livestock and horses, as well as examinations such as multiple-choice and essay questions. You’ll also complete presentations, both individually and in small groups, along with written work including essays, technical reports and your dissertation. Other forms of assessment include seminars, case studies, experimental work, laboratory reports, poster presentations and debates. What equipment will I need? You’ll need a laptop, along with standard safety equipment for outdoor work. This includes steel toe-capped boots or wellingtons, long-sleeved overalls and a waterproof jacket and trousers. The estimated cost is between £100 and £250. You’ll also need notebook and paper for note taking, pens, pencils folders and a scientific calculator. You’ll have the opportunity to participate in optional animal and conservation trips, both locally and overseas. Please note that these trips are self-funded at your own expense. Additional course costs The following equipment and materials are essential (unless stated otherwise), and you'll be using them from the start of your course: white laboratory coat wellies steel toe capped boots waterproofs and appropriate outdoor clothing – for wet weather, lambing etc overalls (not orange) riding hat or skull cap that meets current safety standards. The current BHS-recognised standards are EN1384:1996 with CE mark, BSEN1384:1997 with CE mark, PAS015:2011 with BSI kitemark, ASTM F1163:2004a with SEI mark, E2001 with Snell certification label and AS/NZ 3838:2006 with SAI global mark) gloves that can be worn to protect hands while leading animals (riding gloves ideal but woolly gloves will be fine) you might find a digital camera/smart phone useful for taking photos/videos during practical sessions You'll also need the following study materials: laptop/device pens and pencils notebook or paper for note-taking folders clipboard Living costs Living at university We understand that affordability is an important issue when you’re thinking about studying at university. The overall cost of university can vary depending on where you’re studying and which course you’re taking. Costs may also be lower if you're living at home. However, some of the main costs you’ll want to think about include: accommodation bills internet, mobile phone and calls travel food and drink socialising and going out study materials. Most full-time UK students can apply for a Maintenance Loan to help cover living costs. More about maintenance loans . We also have a range of offers to help with the cost of living . Our Money Advice Service is on hand if you’d like to chat about living costs, budgets and managing your money. You can also find out more about student finance at one of our Open Days . Bursaries, scholarships and part-time work We offer a range of scholarships and bursaries for UK and international students , which provide extra financial support while you’re at university. If you're eligible for a scholarship, you'll generally receive it automatically – there's no need to apply. Our campus employment bureau, ARU Temps , can help you find part-time work that fits around your studies (including any time you may spend on placements). It's a great chance to enhance your CV and boost your income while you study. Source: NSS 2026 Explore a variety of animation and illustration methods and media, including puppet making and stop-motion animation, traditional 2D animation, digital 2D and 3D animation, character and graphic novel design. With guidance and support from dedicated industry professionals, you’ll develop your technical skills and a personal language within animation. You’ll learn the entire creative process from observational drawing and research to storyboarding to editing and sound design, so that you can best bring your characters and stories to life. Follow our course on instagram . This is what studying art and design at ARU actually feels like. Close full-screen gallery. This is what studying art and design at ARU actually feels like. Why ARU? Become a skilled and versatile 2D or 3D animator, focusing on illustration and storytelling Go on group drawing trips and visit museums, galleries and animation festivals Work in dedicated animation production studios with high-end 3D CGI, Cintiqs and rostrum equipment Attend lectures from top animation studios in London Graduate industry-ready with a professional portfolio, showreel or website Get full training on all our facilities, including our print studio and Futures Lab Designed for creative life Our Creative Quarter brings together studios, workshops, performance and exhibition spaces. Be part of a community built around making, experimentation and innovation, while developing your practical skills and portfolio, and connecting with industry. Careers The course makes it easy to make industry connections. They invite guests for live briefs and also provide help with employment. Ruta Stalmokaite, BA (Hons) Animation and Illustration graduate and RTA Student Television Awards 2023 finalist. As a student at ARU you’ll prepare for your future career by creating a showreel, website and promotional material. You'll also take part in a final-year degree show, and attend guest talks from top animation studios such as Passion Pictures, The Mill, FrameStore and Studio Aka. You’ll also get the opportunity to work on live briefs set by industry; we’ve worked with companies like 9 Trees, Provide CIC, Curveball Media, and even the Royal National Lifeboat Institution, creating an animated ident to promote their collaboration with Chelsea Flower Show. What can you do with an Animation and Illustration degree? This degree will prepare you for work in the creative industries a 2D/3D animator, motion graphics designer, or illustrator for a wide range of studios and publishers when you graduate. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You might stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our renowned MA Children’s Book Illustration . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. Where have other Animation and Illustration graduates worked? Many of our graduates now work with leading animation studios and broadcasters such as The Mill, 12 Foot 6, Slurpy Studios, The Like Minded, Filofax, BBC and Channel 4, as well as developing freelance careers in animation and illustration. What have other Animation and Illustration graduates achieved? Madelen Schønningsen won Best Animation for her short animation Lossnord at the 2025 LGBTQ+ Toronto Film Festival . Graduate Hannah Lane’s short animated film A Snowy Surprise was shortlisted for the Cinemagic Film Festival Young Filmmaker Award, as well as being selected for Our Culture and the Bitesize Film Festival. Steven Goodison’s short film Wee Shadows was selected for screening at @FrightFest UK and various other festivals, and Velina Garabedyan's film Wherever I Wander was selected for screening at five festivals. Graduate Sabine Buhain received industry recognition at New Designers – open to all final year visual communication students in the UK – winning the Aardman Academy Screening Award for Like It Was Yesterday . Sabine’s animation grabbed the judges’ attention with her "wonderful design and colour journey [creating] a world we immediately loved". Where have other Animation and Illustration students found work experience? We’ll help you raise your industry profile through exhibitions and awards, and build a strong body of work ready for a professional career in animation. You’ll receive ongoing support to find placements and work, and can also take an optional placement year. Student Hannah Wadsworth chose our placement year option, and worked at The Walt Disney Company in London. Discover more about how the placement helped her . As well as the work presented below, check out the short films our students produced for Provide CIC , BBC Radio 4's The Listening Project , BBC Cambridgeshire , the Globe Theatre , and the New Designers Screening Prize . See more work by graduating students on our Creative Showcase , and follow our students' projects, prizes and progress on Instagram . How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules You’ll learn a broad set of skills and experiment with many methods and themes in both digital and analogue media. Jeff Crosby, Course Director Year 1 is your chance to explore, learn, experiment, and find your unique style. You’ll get straight into the studio, learning the principles of image creation, storytelling, different types of animation, film-making and production methods. In years 2 and 3 you’ll develop your animation and drawing skills and style, and start thinking about your future career by taking part in live projects, creating a website, showreel or portfolio, and building your professional network. Finally, you’ll showcase your abilities and skills as a creative producer with a major individual or group project. Student work Our student showcase Watch our 2026 animation showreel. Placements typically happen in Year 3, and your course will take four years overall. Find out more about placement years . Year 1 Foundation in Art and Design Year 2 Animation Skills Illustration and Animation Practice Sequential Practice Sequential Structures and Contexts Year 3 Animation Practice Computer Generated Imagery Critical Issues and Debates Ruskin Module (15 credits) Year 4 Professional Sequential Practice Working in the Creative Industries * Research Project * Module details What happens on a foundation year? A foundation year prepares you for the rest of your course, and focuses on general skills such as researching and referencing, numeracy and ICT, and communication. We'll also start to look at some more subject-specific topics. What happens on a placement year? Your placement year is a chance to put everything you’ve learnt in Years 1 and 2 into practice. Spend typically 9-12 months working for an organisation, developing your skills and gaining valuable work experience. Our Placements Team is here to help you secure a placement. How is Animation and Illustration assessed? This is a hands-on, practical course and our assessment is based on the coursework you complete for each of your modules. This includes completed project work as well as accompanying material such as sketchbooks, animatics, storyboards, pre-viz, digital tests and rough cuts. Through a blog and discussion we are looking to see how you research, analyse and develop your work – in other words, how you think as a visual artist as well as how you are developing your personal voice, creative expression, production skills and technical know-how. You’ll also attend lectures in which you explore historical and contemporary illustration and animation and current social contexts, and show your research skills and critical thinking in discussions, presentations and written assignments. What equipment will I need? See our recommended materials and things you can do to prepare for the course . Who teaches Animation and Illustration at ARU? Undergraduate BSc (Hons) Applied Psychology Develop your scientific, analytical and research skills and prepare for an exciting career in psychology. Study part-time by distance learning. Our course pages need JavaScript enabled to work correctly. Previous Section Course Overview Next Section Jump to a section Course overview Careers Teaching and modules Entry requirements Fees and funding Apply Apply now Contact our Distance Learning team Start date September 2027 Location Distance learning Award BSc (Hons) Duration 4 years part-time Find out how psychology affects everything we do, influencing our thoughts, feelings and behaviours. Our course takes in applied, social, clinical and biological psychology, cognitive neuroscience and much more. You’ll learn how to conduct research, getting hands-on by setting up experiments and questionnaires, analysing data, and writing reports to a professional standard. Study part-time through distance learning, and develop the scientific, analytical and research skills you need to work as a psychologist. Find out more on our distance learning website . British Psychological Society This course is accredited by the British Psychological Society , meaning you'll graduate with the most up-to-date knowledge and skills in the field of psychology. Why ARU? Study 100% online using our learning management system. Learn from experienced and passionate professionals. Build a foundation for specialising in a range of areas, such as forensic, neuro, clinical, and educational psychology. Gain professional recognition with a course accredited by the British Psychological Society. Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers I found ARU a welcoming and diverse community. I'm very career orientated and was given the opportunity to get involved in research right from day one. Farah, Distance learning student Develop the academic and professional skills you need for a career in psychology and related fields. You could work in areas including: forensic psychology neuropsychology clinical psychology healthcare academia/research teaching counselling. Visit the careers section of the British Psychological Society website to explore the options our Applied Psychology degree could open up for you. Graduation doesn't have to be the end of your time with us. You could develop a specialism or start a career in research with a Masters degree . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. Teaching and modules Discover the history of psychology and how the mind and behaviour are understood now, with reference to cognitive psychology and cognitive neuroscience. You'll learn about mental health problems, formulation and diagnosis, and the main methods of intervention used by clinical, counselling and health psychologists. You'll also gain an insight into symptoms and prognosis for a variety of developmental disorders, and issues involved in assessment and diagnosis. Research is an important part of this course. You’ll learn to review literature, design experiments and studies, analyse data, and write reports. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Source: GOS 2026 Our BSc (Hons) Applied Computer Science (Top Up) course is an exciting opportunity to progress your qualification and gain a full honours degree. You’ll gain hands-on experience in our cutting-edge labs, using industry-standard tools from Microsoft and VMware. Additionally, you’ll develop technical and teamwork skills while becoming a creative problem-solver who's aware of social, moral and ethical issues relating to the impact of computers on our lives. This top-up degree opens pathways to careers in software development, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and a wide range of other IT and computing fields. Why ARU? Progress your current qualification to a BSc (Hons) in Applied Computer Science through this focused top-up programme. Study in Cambridge’s Silicon Fen, a global tech home to Apple, Microsoft, Samsung AI and many more. Bring the world of work to life through Live Briefs ; designed and developed with regional employers, such as Redgate and Citisoft to give you exposure to ‘real world’ experiences. Engage with a curated selection of training materials, providing you with cutting-edge knowledge and skills that align with industry standards. Study at an award-winning university We were named Times Higher Education University of the Year 2023 . We've also been awarded a Gold rating in the Teaching Excellence Framework – a reflection of the outstanding education we offer our students. Careers This course prepares you for a diverse range of IT careers by combining core computer science with specialisations like software development, cloud applications and network support. You'll gain valuable technical and professional skills through hands-on projects, industry-informed modules, and employer engagement. With guest lectures, sponsored projects and the option to earn CCNA certification, you'll graduate well-prepared for the fast-moving tech industry and confident in your ability to thrive in the workplace. Graduation doesn’t have to be the end of your time with us. You might decide to stay at ARU and study for a Masters, such as our MSc Computer Science or MSc Artificial Intelligence . Take advantage of our Alumni Scholarship and get 20% off your fees. What can you do with an Applied Computer Science degree? Graduates from of this course can pursue a wide range of careers across the IT and tech industry, such as: Software Developer / Engineer AI / Machine Learning Specialist Cyber Security Analyst Cloud Solutions Architect Network Administrator / Engineer Technical Support Specialist Web or App Developer How can ARU help with my employability and career development? We want you to be a step ahead when you graduate, so we offer: courses designed with employers tutors with professional industry knowledge hands-on learning through Live Briefs , internships and placements Ruskin Modules that help develop the skills employers value. Alongside your course, there are lots of other opportunities to build your skills and experience: add value to your CV with an ARU Certificate of Professional Development get involved in a thriving volunteering programme develop your brilliant business ideas work with businesses to make a social impact . We’re here to help you develop your CV and find that all-important role after graduation. Our Employability Service offers tailored career appointments, advice on writing your CV, help to complete job applications, and much more. You’ll have 24/7 access to an online Careers Centre too, which is packed with useful resources. The support continues after you graduate, with lifelong access to our Alumni Career Centre . Find out more about careers support at ARU . Teaching and modules Explore the ‘how’ and ‘why’ of tech—building software, experimenting with AI and strengthening cyber defences in every project. Razvan-Ioan Dinita, Senior Lecturer This course covers critical topics in computing, including professional ethics, legal issues, AI, image processing, cybersecurity, cloud computing and a final-year research project. You'll explore areas like data protection, AI algorithms and image recognition using tools like Python. You’ll develop practical skills through coding, cloud infrastructure, security analysis and guided lab work. The final project enhances your research and development skills, preparing you for industry demands. Overall, the course fosters technical, ethical and professional expertise relevant to IT, engineering, and computing careers. What will I study? Modules are subject to change and availability, and may vary by location. If you have the choice of optional modules, these are indicated with a *. Year 1 Final Project (30 credits) Professional Issues: Computing and Society (15 credits) Artificial Intelligence (15 credits) Image Processing (15 credits) Security Management, Operations and Analytics (30 credits) Cloud Computing (15 credits) Module details How is Applied Computer Science assessed? Throughout the course we’ll use a range of assessment methods to help measure your progress. Besides exams, these will include group work, presentations, case studies, laboratory tests and projects. What equipment will I need? You will need your own laptop for this course (focusing on as much processing power, RAM, and storage capacity as possible). Who teaches Applied Computer Science at ARU? Read profiles of teaching and research staff on this course.
